Summarise the main differences between TCP and UDP for a network course.

TCP is connection oriented: a three-way handshake opens the connection, every segment is acknowledged, lost segments are retransmitted and the receiver gets the bytes in order. Flow control (the receive window) and congestion control (slow start, congestion avoidance) keep the sender from overwhelming the network.

UDP sends independent datagrams with no handshake, no acknowledgement, no ordering and no retransmission. It has a smaller header and no connection state, which suits DNS queries, streaming media, voice and games where a late packet is worth less than a lost one.

In short: choose TCP when every byte must arrive in order, UDP when latency matters more than completeness.
